purpose: make sure the product works for users on the browsers and versions that matter, based on who actually uses it
entry_criteria: Analytics or customer data on browser use exist
Access to the browsers or a cloud grid exists
procedure: Build the support matrix from real usage data and the support policy: browser, version range and operating system.
Rank the matrix by usage and risk, and decide which combinations get full tests and which get a smoke check.
Run the core journeys on each tier, using automation where it exists and manual checks for layout and input behavior.
Compare layout, fonts, forms, media and scripts, and note where features degrade without breaking the task.
Record each difference with browser, version, steps and a screenshot, and decide to fix, work around or document.
Review the matrix whenever usage shifts or a new browser release changes the picture.
deliverables: decisions on fixes or documented limits
acceptance_criteria: The matrix is based on usage data
Core journeys passed on each top tier
Differences have evidence and a decision
The matrix has a review date

validation.expect: core journeys pass on all projects

validation.check: open the checkout on the oldest supported version of each browser

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: Usage data places four browsers above 5 percent each; those get full journey runs, the others a smoke check. A date picker is found to behave differently in one version and gets a workaround.
